sentence_stem: Had the company listened to its customers,
correct_completion: it would not be losing money today.
full_sentence: Had the company listened to its customers, it would not be losing money today.
acceptable_variants: it would not be losing money now.
it would be more profitable today.

options.text: it is not losing money today.
options.why_wrong: The present tense states a real fact. It does not express the imagined present result of a past condition that did not happen.

options.text: it would not be losing money today.
it did not lose money last year.
options.why_wrong: The past simple states a past fact. It does not express the present result of an unreal past condition.

options.text: it would not have lost money now.
options.why_wrong: The perfect form points to the past, which conflicts with 'now'. Mixed conditionals connect a past condition to a present result.

grammar_focus: Mixed conditionals with inverted 'had' (past condition, present result)
explanation: 'Had the company listened' is an inverted form of 'If the company had listened', which is a mixed conditional. The past condition leads to a present result, so 'would' plus a base verb is needed. Portuguese speakers may choose a past form here because the inverted word order is less familiar to them, so the subject-verb inversion is easy to overlook.
translation: Se a empresa tivesse ouvido os seus clientes, hoje não estaria perdendo dinheiro.
